comments.flawless: Joshua: The report was right on the first try. Bonus approved.
comments.done: Joshua: Case closed. Next time, look at the sender's domain and at where the link really goes before you decide.

all_clues_monologue: That's enough. A look-alike domain made two days ago sent a link that says one address and goes to another, and one person typed his password.
The real IT notice and HR's link look just as official. Time to press REPORT and spot what was fake in the message.

email.title: EMAIL > THE MESSAGE, THE FORWARD, THE REAL ONES

entries.title: Your password expires today, from c0mpany-it.com
entries.detail:
From: IT Support <it@c0mpany-it.com>
To: 40 staff
Time: today 09:12
Subject: Your password expires today

Dear colleague, your password expires today. Sign in now at portal.company-it.com to keep it.

Look at the sender's domain: c0mpany-it.com has a zero where the o of company should be.
monologue: The sender says IT, and the domain has a zero where the o should be. It is easy to read it wrong.
Would you spot that at a glance?
entries.summary: The email came at 09:12 from c0mpany-it.com, with a zero for an o.

entries.title: Is this real?
entries.detail:
From: Tessa Brandt, front desk
To: IT desk

I got this email that says my password expires today. It looks like IT, but it feels hurried. I did not click. Is it real?
monologue: Tessa did not click, and she asked. That is the best thing anyone did this morning.
Who else got it, and who did click?
entries.summary: Tessa asked IT about the email at 09:40, before she clicked.
